strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear identification of limitations in existing paradigms for small VLMs (pseudo thinking traces and advantage collapse)
Clear presentation and effective visualizations that communicate the key ideas and problems
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across three diverse domains with multiple SVLM baselines and LVLM comparisons
Solid empirical results showing consistent improvements (e.g., SmolVLM +5.7%, +6.5% on charts) and competitive performance with larger models
Reasonable ablation study demonstrating contribution of dynamic selection mechanism and visual supervision components
Practical value for edge deployment scenarios where small models with reasoning are needed
Gradient compatibility analysis (Eqs. 4-5) providing theoretical motivation for SFT-GRPO integration
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core contribution (dynamic SFT-GRPO switching via binary correctness threshold) is conceptually straightforward and lacks exploration of alternative strategies
Unfair experimental comparisons: baseline methods lack visual checker/refiner modules, making it unclear whether improvements stem from dynamic switching or visual supervision
Heavy dependence on domain-specific visual fact extraction tools (BiomedGPT, DePlot, manual collection), severely limiting practical applicability and reproducibility
Vague technical specifications for key components: visual checker/refiner implementations described as 'prompt engineering' without concrete details on computation, templates, or thresholds
Missing reproducibility details: no code availability mentioned, hyperparameters not justified, visual refiner templates unspecified, no error bars or significance testing
Simple binary decision rule (any correct response?) lacks theoretical justification and ablation; no exploration of alternative selection mechanisms
Limited statistical rigor: single-run results without confidence intervals or significance tests; modest improvements on capable models (InternVL2-S +1.8%) raise generality questions
Incomplete ablations: missing ablation giving baselines visual supervision; no ablation isolating dynamic mechanism from visual modules
Evaluation limited to rule-based verification tasks on extractive QA; generalization to open-ended reasoning and other task types unclear
Overstated novelty claims: claims to 'first enable' thinking in SVLMs when method primarily improves existing capabilities; concurrent related work (R1-V, etc.) not clearly differentiated

strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear practical importance for edge-device deployment of VLMs
Consistent empirical improvements across three different domains and multiple SVLM architectures (0.5B-1B parameters)
Clear presentation with effective visualizations communicating the core ideas intuitively
Comprehensive evaluation scope covering recognition-intensive to reasoning-intensive tasks
Gradient compatibility analysis (Section 3.1) provides mathematical grounding for combining SFT and GRPO
Ablation study (Table 3) demonstrates contribution of individual components
weaknesses: Core decision mechanism (Eq. 6) is oversimplified—binary threshold on answer correctness with no consideration of confidence, diversity, or intermediate step quality; lacks justification for why this rule is optimal

Critical methodological issue: Heavy dependence on external visual supervision (BiomedGPT, DePlot, manual collection) that is not transparently evaluated; unclear how much improvement comes from this supervision vs. the dynamic switching mechanism
Visual checker/refiner implementation critically underspecified: 'soft recall-based relevance score' is never formally defined; insufficient detail for reproducibility
Insufficient analysis of two-stage baseline: SmolVLM gap of 10+ points (45.4→55.6) is dramatic but unexplained; unclear if baselines received equal hyperparameter tuning
Limited novelty: Dynamic switching between objectives is straightforward; SFT+RL combinations already explored; the contribution is primarily an engineering combination of known techniques
Data reuse concern: Table 1 notes datasets were 'already introduced during pre-training,' raising questions about test-set contamination and fair evaluation
No ablation isolating external supervision contribution; cannot determine whether improvements come from the switching mechanism or additional visual signal

Missing critical implementation details: predefined template design, visual fact source construction per domain, training curves beyond geometry, computational cost analysis, hyperparameter sensitivity
No statistical significance testing: no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests provided; single-run improvements lack rigor
Incomplete baseline comparisons: limited comparison with other recent SVLM reasoning approaches; potential cherry-picking when claiming competitiveness with LVLMs
Removal of KL penalty and clipping from standard GRPO (p. 6) justified only by assertion that 'SFT stabilizing effect overlaps'—not formally proven
Inconsistent domain performance (InternVL2-S geometry: only +1.1% vs. +4.3% for SmolVLM) without explanation of variation
Computational overhead not discussed: K-sample generation per step adds cost; efficiency claims require analysis given SVLM emphasis on deployment efficiency
Limited qualitative analysis: only 2 examples in Figure 5; no systematic investigation of reasoning step grounding, failure modes, or when method struggles

strengths: Well-motivated problem: clearly identifies limitations of existing training paradigms for SVLMs with concrete examples and quantitative evidence
Clear presentation: excellent visualizations (Figures 1-3) effectively communicate core ideas; well-structured paper with logical flow
Principled approach: gradient compatibility analysis (Eq. 4-5) provides sound mathematical justification for integrating SFT and GRPO
Comprehensive experiments: evaluation across three domains (medical VQA, chart QA, geometry), three SVLM architectures, and includes ablation study demonstrating necessity of each component
Consistent and strong empirical results: improvements across all models (+1.8% to +5.7%) and domains; DyME-trained SVLMs achieve parity with stronger LVLMs (e.g., 0.5B model outperforms 10B model)
Practical value: addresses real need for efficient edge-deployable models without adding parameters; directly applicable to practitioners
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core contribution is straightforward—dynamically switch between SFT and RLVR based on binary correctness criterion. Lacks algorithmic depth expected at top-tier venues

Fairness of baseline comparisons: two-stage baseline lacks implementation details; no evidence of equivalent hyperparameter tuning; unclear whether performance gaps reflect fundamental differences or suboptimal tuning

Domain-specific visual components: relies on external tools (BiomedGPT, DePlot, manual collection) for visual fact extraction; visual refiner uses ad-hoc manually-designed/iteratively-adapted templates; severely limits generalizability to new domains

Insufficient experimental rigor: single runs without error bars or significance testing; missing crucial details (template construction, group size K, learning rates, batch sizes, training steps); no computational cost analysis despite using 16 V100 GPUs

Simplistic decision rule without justification: binary threshold (Eq. 6) used without exploring alternative criteria; no ablation on decision rule itself (e.g., >50% correct); claim about narrow feasible training range (Fig. 1b) stated qualitatively but never quantitatively validated

Limited scope of evaluation: all three tasks are structured-output/reasoning tasks requiring rule-based verification; unclear generalization to open-ended generation, captioning, or other VLM tasks without verifiable answers
Visual facts extraction scalability: geometry facts manually collected; severe reproducibility and scalability concerns; no guidance for practitioners on applying method to new domains

Incomplete training analysis: limited discussion of stability edge cases, recovery from poor optima, or whether dynamic switching provides advantage over careful fixed curriculum; simplified GRPO without KL/clipping may limit generalizability

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing genuine limitations of SVLMs with clear empirical demonstration
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple domains, models, and datasets with thorough ablations and human evaluation
Consistent and meaningful empirical improvements (+4-6% across multiple SVLM architectures) with SVLMs matching/exceeding some LVLMs on specialized tasks
Practical contribution addressing real deployment needs for efficient edge models
Thoughtfully designed visual supervision components with clear design rationale for handling SVLM constraints
Strong reproducibility efforts with detailed prompts, protocols, and evaluation across new domains
weaknesses: Limited novelty of core mechanism: binary dynamic switching based on correctness is straightforward; combining SFT and RLVR is well-explored, making the contribution incremental over prior two-stage and annealed loss approaches

Visual supervision introduces significant complexity and external dependencies (LLM APIs for prompt engineering, domain-specific tools like DePlot) that limit applicability and reproducibility, with ~1.6× computational overhead

Experimental design concerns: (1) two-stage baselines perform surprisingly poorly without clear evidence of equivalent tuning effort; (2) Part II improvements may conflate data refinement gains from visual refiner with switching mechanism benefits

Limited evaluation scope restricted to structured/semi-structured domains where visual facts are easily extractable; acknowledged limitations for abstract visuals significantly narrow practical applicability
Reasoning quality limitations: fixed template-based thinking trades flexibility for stability; human evaluation shows 28-32% of generated traces remain problematic; failure modes not analyzed
Insufficient analysis of switching dynamics during training and lack of theoretical justification for why the specific binary rule should outperform continuous weighting alternatives
Key technical choices lack justification: removing KL penalty and clipping from GRPO needs validation; visual checker score-to-reward conversion unclear; sensitivity analysis missing
Cold start problem not addressed: how does training behave in early stages when model rarely generates correct responses?

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing practical need for efficient SVLMs with reasoning capabilities
Clear problem diagnosis with effective visualizations showing failure modes of existing paradigms
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across three diverse domains with thorough ablation studies
Consistent empirical improvements across multiple SVLM architectures
Extensive supplementary materials with human evaluation and additional analyses
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: core contribution is a simple binary switching heuristic rather than fundamental innovation
Unfair baseline comparisons: DyME receives external supervision via Qwen2.5-14B vision facts while baselines do not, making comparisons non-equivalent
Heavy reliance on external large models contradicts core goal of empowering small models; Full DyME incurs 1.6× computational overhead
Narrow and domain-specific applicability: requires structured visual semantics, rule-based verifiable answers, and cannot handle abstract reasoning tasks
Lack of statistical rigor: no error bars, confidence intervals, significance tests, or multiple random seeds reported
Unfair baseline tuning: two-stage training is hyperparameter-sensitive but no systematic hyperparameter search shown for baselines
Marginal improvements on realistic models: InternVL2-S shows only +1.8% gain, suggesting limited scalability
Incomplete vision supervision analysis: no sensitivity studies to visual facts quality or robustness to different extraction methods
Limited human evaluation: only 100 samples from one domain; missing evaluation on medical VQA and geometry
Poor absolute performance on some tasks: geometry solving remains at 18.9% on SmolVLM even with DyME, indicating limited effectiveness

strengths: Well-motivated problem: Clearly articulates why existing SFT and RLVR paradigms fail for SVLMs, with concrete examples (pseudo thinking traces, advantage collapse)
Simple, elegant core mechanism: The binary switching rule is parameter-free and addresses hyperparameter sensitivity that plagues static SFT-RL trade-offs

Comprehensive experimental validation: Two-part structure (algorithmic validation + system effectiveness), rigorous ablations, human evaluation of CoT quality, and testing across multiple SVLMs and domains
Practical significance: Demonstrates SVLMs can match/exceed larger models on specialized tasks, with real implications for edge deployment of vision-language models
Consistent empirical improvements: Shows gains across diverse domains and multiple model scales (SmolVLM +5.7%, LLaVA-OV-S +4.7%, InternVL2-S +1.8%)
Transparent presentation and reproducibility: Extensive supplementary materials with implementation details, full prompts, additional experiments, and human evaluation results
Strong ablation studies: Table 3 clearly decomposes contributions of memorization mode (20.6% drop), exploration mode (9.0% drop), visual components (4.7-6.9% drops)
weaknesses: Limited novelty of core mechanism: The binary switching rule is straightforward; combining SFT and GRPO with a simple heuristic lacks theoretical depth and insight into why this particular design should be optimal

Heavy dependence on external LLMs undermines 'empowering small models' narrative: Visual supervision requires Qwen2.5-14B; this creates 1.6× training overhead (Table 4) and makes improvements partially attributable to better data rather than algorithmic innovation

Unfair comparison setup: Baselines lack access to external LLM-based visual supervision during training; improvements conflate data quality gains with algorithmic contributions. Needs clear ablation separating these factors

Severe applicability constraints for visual supervision module: Fails on abstract reasoning (memes, cultural context); requires domain-specific visual fact extraction (DePlot, BiomedGPT); limits generality claims despite multi-domain testing
Limited improvements on stronger models: InternVL2-S shows only +1.8% gain; suggests method primarily addresses data/capacity limitations of weak models rather than fundamental reasoning limitations

Narrow generalization evidence: Small training sets (4-6K samples), all task-specific; unclear if scalable to general-purpose scenarios. A-OKVQA and GSM8K experiments relegated to supplementary and feel secondary

Insufficient decomposition of contributions: Visual supervision complexity rivals the algorithmic contribution; unclear whether improvements come from dynamic switching vs. better supervised data from external LLMs

Missing theoretical justification: No analysis of convergence properties, optimality of switching criterion, or conditions under which binary switching might fail. Gradient compatibility (Eqs. 4-5) is straightforward and expected

Incomplete comparison with related methods: CHORD and LUFFY only discussed in supplementary; missing main-paper discussion of how DyME theoretically differs from these alternative dynamic weighting approaches

Reproducibility challenges for new domains: Visual fact extraction is non-trivial and domain-specific; geometry facts are 'collected' rather than automated; not easily plug-and-play despite generality claims
